Never cancel a credit card. If you want to, just pay it all off and cut it up. You want to keep it open though bc it adds to the average age of your credit. Many will be automatically closed after a certain period of inactivity.

I think the article gives a pretty balanced treatment of the cancel versus don't cancel issue. For somebody with a few current cards that they rarely use, yes, they probably shouldn't cancel them because there's very little harm or risk... for someone who compulsively purchases things on credit however, it may be much more beneficial to cancel them. In addition to the short treatment in the actual article, there's also a link to a more expanded treatment of the issue.

one thing about keeping old cards around is you probably want to make sure they're still being used, as companies may be tempted to cancel a card that goes completely unused for an extended period of time. I have a credit card that I haven't used to make a purchase in longer than I can remember, nor carried with me, but it is the one hooked up to my Netflix subscription so it will remain open and demonstrating that I have old, hardly utilized lines of credit.

Linking it to Netflix is a really good idea. I like that. I have one that I use just for gas for a similar reason. Every month the payment is roughly the same and never causes me any issues, and I know I'll keep using it every month.

Second this. Keep the card.

If it's a rewards card keep it and take advantage of the rewards.

I get a lot of benefits from my card. After I got it in the mail I got a ~100 page booklet with tiny type, I figured it was just a bunch of legal shit, nope, it was hundreds of benefits. If I rent a car with the card they automatically insure the card with 0 deductible, every item I purchase with the card that has a warranty, the card doubles the manufacturer warranty (except vehicles). It has roadside assistance so I can drop AAA. Free currency exchange rate. The list goes on and on,

And then the reward points. Talking $1,000's of dollars in free travel, free hotels, and free car rentals in only a few years. If you are responsible enough to not abuse it and pay it off every month you can really come out ahead with a good rewards card.

If it's just a regular old card keep if for these reasons.

  1. It will report on time payments which really help your credit score

  2. It will keep your available credit to debt ratio high, good for your credit

  3. In case of an emergency you know you always have a little extra lying around

Other than that I thought it was a pretty good article. I just disagree with getting rid of your credit card simply to "get rid of your credit cards"
